chief_complaint: rash on my face, joint pain, and fatigue
hpi_details: 28F presents with 3 weeks of a sun-sensitive red rash across her cheeks and nose. She also reports severe fatigue, achy joints (wrists, knees), and painless ulcers in her mouth.
ideas: thinks she has a weird allergy
expectations: wants a cream and blood test

core_concepts: Multisystem autoimmune disease affecting young women.
Classic triad: malar rash, joint pain, fatigue.
Other signs: photosensitivity, oral ulcers, serositis, renal disease.
common_misconceptions: Confusing malar rash with rosacea (rosacea often involves nasolabial folds).
dangerous_errors: Failing to check for renal involvement (lupus nephritis), which can be silent.
management_principles: Obtain ANA with disease-specific serology as indicated, CBC, renal/liver function, urinalysis with sediment and protein quantification, blood pressure, and prompt rheumatology referral. Treatment is organ- and pregnancy-plan-specific and should be clinician directed.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

source_refs.title: American College of Rheumatology (ACR) Clinical Guidance

reference_soap.subjective: 28F with a new photosensitive facial rash, fatigue, arthralgias, and oral ulcers.
reference_soap.objective: Erythematous rash over cheeks and nasal bridge sparing nasolabial folds. Hard palate ulcers.
reference_soap.plan: Check ANA, anti-dsDNA, anti-Smith, CBC, renal/liver function, urinalysis with sediment and protein quantification, and blood pressure; refer promptly to rheumatology. Counsel on sun protection and seek urgent care for reduced urine, edema, chest pain, breathlessness, severe headache, confusion, or fever.

learning_objectives: Recognize the diverse multiorgan presentation of SLE.

teaching.one_liner: A young female with a photosensitive malar rash, oral ulcers, and inflammatory arthralgias.
red_flags: Foamy or bloody urine, reduced urine output, leg swelling, new hypertension, or breathlessness may indicate organ involvement and needs urgent assessment.

must_ask.say: Does the rash on your face get worse after being out in the sun?
Have you noticed any sores or ulcers in your mouth?
Which joints are achy, and is there any swelling?
Have you noticed your urine looking foamy, or any swelling in your legs?
How long has this been going on, and how severe is the fatigue?

history.answer: I've had this red rash spreading across my cheeks and nose for about three weeks, and my joints have been aching and I feel completely exhausted.
It started about three weeks ago after I spent a sunny weekend outdoors, and it hasn't faded or gone away since then.
The rash is across both of my cheeks and over the bridge of my nose, but the folds around my mouth and the rest of my body are completely clear.
It looks like a flat to slightly bumpy red patch across my face, without any blisters, peeling skin, or crusts.
Yes, whenever I spend even a few minutes outside in the sun, my face becomes much redder and feels like it's burning.
It feels warm and slightly tender in the sun, but it does not really itch.
No, the rash stays there constantly day and night; individual spots do not disappear in a few hours like hives do.
I have never had a facial rash or joint troubles like this before in my life.
I haven't had a fever or chills, but I've been feeling deeply fatigued and run-down no matter how much I sleep.
I noticed a couple of shallow sores on the roof of my mouth about a week ago, though surprisingly they don't hurt when I eat.
No, my eyes aren't red or gritty, and I haven't had any sores in my private area.
No, my skin is not peeling off, and I haven't noticed any dark purple spots that stay when pressed.
No swelling of my lips or tongue, no throat tightness, no trouble breathing, and no lightheadedness.
I haven't started taking any new prescription medications, antibiotics, or painkillers recently.
No, I haven't changed my face creams, makeup, laundry soaps, or worn any new jewelry.
No one at home or work has a rash or any illness like this.
I was at an outdoor park three weeks ago, but I don't recall any bug bites, tick bites, or hikes in tall weeds.
I've never had asthma, eczema, or allergic rhinitis.
Both of my wrists and both knees feel sore and stiff, especially in the morning when I first get out of bed.
My nails look normal, though I have noticed a bit more hair coming out in my brush over the last month.
I tried an over-the-counter hydrocortisone cream on my cheeks for three days, but it didn't improve the rash at all.
My urine looks normal yellow, not foamy or red, and I haven't noticed any change in how much I pee.
No, my feet and ankles look normal and haven't swollen up.
I am in a monogamous relationship with my partner, and neither of us has ever had genital sores or infections.
I was wondering if I developed some sort of unusual allergy to sunlight or pollen.
I'm really worried about my face and whether this red rash will leave permanent marks or keep spreading.
I'm hoping to get a prescription cream to calm my skin down and maybe run a blood test to figure out what's causing it.
I have always been healthy and have never been diagnosed with any chronic medical conditions.
I have never had surgery and I've never been admitted to a hospital.
I don't take any daily prescription drugs, over-the-counter pills, or vitamins.
I don't have any allergies to medications, foods, or anything else that I know of.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used electronic cigarettes.
I only have an occasional glass of wine when out with friends, maybe once or twice a month.
I work as an administrative assistant at an office, and I live in an apartment with my partner.
My mother has a thyroid condition, but no one in my family has lupus, psoriasis, or rheumatoid arthritis.
My last period started two weeks ago, my periods are regular every 28 days, we use condoms, and there is no chance I am pregnant.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 118/76 mmHg, heart rate 78 beats/min, respiratory rate 16 breaths/min, body temperature 37.1°C, oxygen saturation 99% on ambient air.
Alert young female appearing mildly fatigued, sitting comfortably in no acute distress.

Well-demarcated confluent erythematous maculopapular rash across bilateral cheeks and the bridge of the nose sparing the nasolabial folds; no skin peeling, flaking, or crusting; no rash on trunk or extremities; nail beds and scalp appear normal.
Two shallow, non-bleeding, painless ulcers on the hard palate; posterior pharynx clear without tonsillar exudate.
Conjunctivae pink and clear without injection, exudate, or subconjunctival hemorrhage; sclerae non-icteric.
No palpable lymphadenopathy in the anterior cervical, posterior cervical, supraclavicular, or axillary chains; thyroid gland normal in size.
Normal S1 and S2 heart sounds, regular rate and rhythm, without murmurs, rubs, or gallops.
Clear breath sounds throughout all lung fields bilaterally without wheezing, crackles, or pleural friction rub.
Mild tenderness on palpation and passive range of motion across bilateral wrists and knees, without visible swelling, warmth, redness, or joint effusion.
No pretibial or ankle edema bilaterally.
